item.p: wasm-1 done: sxml.wasm built and its package run here for the first time since 7.28, 7.29, fix-7 and perf-17. Setup: wasi-sdk-34 (the version mise.toml pins) at /opt/wasi-sdk, the toolchain file's default; Node.js v22.22.0; the book's JavaScript chapters need WASI_SDK_PREFIX=/opt/wasi-sdk for the language module's clang line. One failure, fixed (e68e524): 7.29's locations test compared Value.toString() (adaptive, so "2") with 2. Now ctest's javascript/package 26/26, languages 30/30 (Schematron with warnings and documents), streams 22/22 (locations), code_languages 10/10, typecheck and size_budget pass: sxml.wasm 13,833,376 stripped, 2,529,416 gzipped (limit 14,000,000 / 2,800,000, not raised; +406,889 since the baseline, most perf-17's tables: xpath_full_text +63,754, value_template +49,064, xpath +49,044, xslt_pattern +48,030, and schematron_build +57,028); the CLI module 15,441,066 / 2,817,989 (15,500,000 / 2,900,000). Book JavaScript examples 7/7; native release ctest 466/466.

fix-7 done (): Schematron queries see xs, fn, math, , and err without ns (the binding annexes); every finding names the document it is in ( in the C report, the command's text and JSON, the package), so a pattern with documents reports the other file with its lines; real rule sets' three known deviations read with schematron:compatibility warnings. Suite 520: 467 pass, 6 deviations (3 new, ); EN 16931 UBL 1,133/1,133 and CII 9/9 from the sources; XRechnung compiles from its sources; the differential against SchXslt identical on the unpatched EN 16931 and XRechnung (255, 128, 226, 128 instances). Book: rules, documents, reports (Warnings), C chapters. sxml.wasm not built (no WASI SDK).

book-30 done: the book's Schematron part, "Checking Rules with Schematron", replaces the invoice chapter. Seven chapters on the Vane projects: where Schematron fits (draft.sch on the draft), the language (review.sch: rule order, visit-each, group, subject, diagnostics, levels), the state machine's checks of check.xq as flag.sch (with phases, #ANY and when, and the typed-value check through xsl:import-schema and an xsl:function with xsl:try), the codegen API's type names checked against vane-api.xsd with --schema and --schematron, abstract patterns, abstract rules, include and a library, reports (text, JSON, SVRL, exit statuses, schema errors, query bindings), and C (schematron.c). No invoice or e-invoicing standard is named in docs/book. All 928 examples match (release build of HEAD, no SXML_JAVASCRIPT); mdbook builds. Found: a finding of a pattern with documents is printed with the FILE's name and the other document's line (text and JSON give no document for it), so the book shows no documents example; and no prefix, not even fn or , is in scope in Schematron expressions without ns.

fix-6 done: the book's memory example (docs/book/src/c.md) counts 194 allocations at HEAD, the same in 30 runs each of the release build and a GCC build with ASan and UBSan, with and without TZ and LANG, from any working directory: stable for one build. It drifted with the library: 195 when book-21 wrote it, 197 from perf-5 (c36c9a547, slices share items), 196 from perf-12 (6433339c9), 194 from perf-16 (c61054355), measured on each of the 33 commits since that changed src, include or CMake. The chapter is built only by tools/check-book-examples.sh, so those commits did not see it. 166 of the 194 come before evaluation; ten squares take 176. The book shows 194, and its prose says "a couple of hundred" instead of repeating the number, which no check reads.

perf-16 done (): IR passes after . Nothing grew faster than the unit; the loop passes walked it about ten times (owners in five passes, a census per function in three, the demand members, a walk per function in fusion), at about 130 instructions per expression. Now the child walk writes in place, the demand pass walks each body once (census and stream marks with the members, no owners), the descendant census comes from the owned expressions, fusion finds its functions in one scan. Invoice validate 1.613 to 1.413 x 10^9 (passes 0.502 to 0.302, demand 0.200 to 0.100), 0.246 to 0.221 s; transform 1.618 to 1.506, 0.214 to 0.202 s; growth N = 256 17.50 to 16.35; xmark-all equal. IR text and item demands identical on EN 16931, the growth series and 414,470 XT40 units; XP40, XQ40, XT40 0 outcomes differ; suite 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133 of 1,133.

perf-17 done (): parsing XPath. A primary expression was reduced once per precedence level (22 hidden rules) before it reached an operand; grammars/xpath now inlines those choice rules (and the steps', primaries' and names'), so an EN 16931 assertion takes 132 reductions, not 676, with the same named nodes (XQuery keeps its tables: +558 KB for a parse made once). An AST memo parses each expression text once per XSLT read or Schematron compile; the walk keeps fields per identifier. Invoice transform 1.618 to 1.291 x 10^9 (-20 %), validate 1.613 to 1.321 (-18 %), XPath parsing 32 % to 14 % of the transform; 0.212 to 0.185 s and 0.246 to 0.219 s; new xpath-parse benchmark 0.947 to 0.649. ASTs identical on 119,276 texts, IR text on EN 16931 and all 414,483 XT40 units; 380 XPath syntax errors are located elsewhere (the CLI and book examples updated). XP40, XQ40, XT40: 0 outcomes differ; suite 463/463, VEFA 1,133/1,133. sxml.wasm (+206 KB of tables) not built here.

fix-5 done (): default priorities of union patterns. XSLT 4.0, 6.4.1 changed 3.0's rule (PR 1772): a union pattern is one rule whose default priority is the minimum of its alternatives', for version="3.0" too (3.8.3). sxml already does this, so the reproduction's "plain plain" is 4.0's answer; a unit test now holds it. XT40 12,185 passed before and after, 0 outcomes differ; suite 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133 of 1,133. next-match-025a, -026a and conflict-resolution-1901a still expect another rule than 6.4.1's.

perf-15 done (): template rules chosen from rule buckets. Each mode indexes its rules by what their pattern may match (node kind, and the expanded name of a name test) in the mode's order; apply-templates, next-match, apply-imports, streamed modes and the built-in templates try only the rules of the item's kind and name plus those that may match any name. Match functions were 88 % of the steps on the EN 16931 invoice. Transform 1.957 to 1.618 x 10^9 instructions (the transform 0.548 to 0.208; steps 1.36 M to 0.32 M), 0.262 to 0.222 s; validate 1.903 to 1.613 (validation 0.479 to 0.189), 0.288 to 0.254 s; new xslt-many-rules 55.8 to 3.4 x 10^9, 7.0 to 0.46 s; xmark-all and XT40's run time unchanged. XT40 12,185, XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114: 0 outcomes differ; SVRL and findings identical over 1,148 files; suite 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133 of 1,133.

perf-14 done (): running compiled Schematron. The compiled Schematron cost twice the official stylesheet on the EN 16931 invoice because its walk visited text nodes (@* | node(), 1,177 nodes per mode against 439), and each visit calls the mode's match functions in rule order: 123,282 match calls against 44,422. A pattern now walks attributes, text, comments and processing instructions only when one of its rule contexts may match them. Validation 1.208 to 0.479 x 10^9 instructions (official 0.548), 0.362 to 0.296 s; VEFA 47.1 to 26.3 x 10^9, 7.5 to 4.7 s; findings byte-identical over 1,150 files; suite 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133 of 1,133. Proposed: a rule search that skips rules by node kind and name, for XSLT too.

perf-13 done (): compiling XSLT and Schematron. XSLT's component graph and bindings find components through indexes made once by sorting (they walked every declaration or instance per reference); a value template without "{" or "}" is its text, built without a parse (5.6.1); the Schematron builder parses each synthesized text once and copies its AST, and checks parameter names by sorting. Invoice transform 2.077 to 1.958 x 10^9 instructions (0.274 to 0.263 s); validate --schematron 3.366 to 2.633 (0.442 to 0.380 s), its compile 2.138 to 1.405; growth N = 256 18.2 to 11.0 (2.39 to 1.62 s), each doubling x 2.02 (was 2.46); xmark-all unchanged. IR text identical (EN 16931, growth, all 414,470 XT40 units); XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185, 0 outcomes differ; Schematron suite 463 of 463, VEFA 1,133 of 1,133, findings byte-identical. Proposed: streamability's mode search and the lowerer's variable lookup still grow with the square of a stylesheet.

perf-12 done (): compiling large stylesheets in linear time, the IR after the passes byte-identical (EN 16931, all 414,483 XT40 units). Three costs grew faster than the unit: the descendant pass scanned the unit once per function, the global-read pass climbed LET chains per expression, and the XPath lowerer checked every global against every other per expression. Then the fusion pass skips functions without a QUANTIFIED, and the XPath front end keeps AST kinds per grammar symbol. Invoice 2.680 to 2.076 x 10^9 instructions (0.386 to 0.305 s); a stylesheet of 1,024 templates 57.1 to 6.2 (4.34 to 0.91 s), each doubling now x 2; xmark-all and SchXslt expand unchanged. XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185, 0 outcomes differ; VEFA 1,133 of 1,133. Proposed: XSLT's component graph is now the cost that grows with the square of a stylesheet.

7.28 done (): Schematron (ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025) as a front end to the XSLT AST. C API, sxml validate --schematron (--phase, --schematron-param, text, JSON, SVRL), the JavaScript compileSchematron (not built here: no WASI SDK), a compile report sink for XSLT (), the driver sxml-schematron-test and a book chapter. 7.30's suite: 463 of 463 applicable normative cases, 3 listed deviations, 43 implementation-defined, 5 refused bindings; one suite case corrected (abstract-in-phase, a duplicate id). EN 16931 UBL unit tests 1,133 of 1,133 from the .sch sources; its compile 0.53 s (SchXslt on sxml: 280 s), 79 MB peak with all 1,131 tests, which run in 9.4 s. Differential against SchXslt: identical findings and fired rules on EN 16931 UBL and, patched, CII and XRechnung UBL and CII. Proposed: EN 16931 CII names a parameter twice and XRechnung relies on SchXslt's leniency (global pattern variables, lets after assertions, an unbound xs). XT40 12,185 passed, 0 outcomes differ.

perf-11 done (): node atomization describes its node once, and string values step over attributes by count. The profile: SchXslt's expand stage atomizes 4,903 distinct untyped nodes 2.71 million times, about 1,010 instructions each, 70 % of it the atomic cell (allocation, UTF-8 validation, type resolution in src/xdm_atomic.c). Expand 47.78 to 47.45 x 10^9 instructions (-0.7 %), coercion.xq 2.716 to 2.695, xmark-all 8.747 to 8.643 (-1.2 %); seconds within noise. QT4 XP40 (32,785), XQ40 (46,114), XT40 (12,185), base and change built and run alike: 0 outcomes differ. The cell's costs are proposed for a later packet ().

fix-4 done (): a choice whose alternatives an item matches none of tries each until one gives an item that matches it (XPath 4.0, 3.4.2), so (element(a) | xs:string) takes xs:untypedAtomic("v") as the string "v"; a caught error no longer stays in the error record (try/catch, finally, template patterns, the filter index), so a later limit is reported alone (, reproduced with a depth limit). QT4 XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185 passed before and after, case by case: 0 outcomes differ. SchXslt expand: same output, same instructions.

perf-10 done (): casts that keep the string relabel the source's cell (xs:untypedAtomic to xs:string 1,650 to 240 instructions), one item against a choice is kept by the first alternative it matches, and untyped items are cast without a match first. SchXslt's expand stage 52.19 to 47.78 x 10^9 instructions (coercion 21 % to 14 %), about 6.7 to 5.9 s; coercion.xq 2.845 to 2.716; xmark-all 8.735 to 8.746. QT4 XP40 (32,785), XQ40 (46,114) and XT40 (12,185) whole, release, case by case: 0 outcomes differ. Left: node atomization (src/xdm_node.c), new vectors matched once per walk, and a choice coercion gap ().

7.29 (): source locations for parsed input documents. The processor setting (AUTOMATIC, ALWAYS, NEVER; additive after ) and sxml_node_get_location (tree.h, additive); one flag per IR unit set where expressions are added (fn:location, fn:function-lookup, fn:load-xquery-module, fn:transform, xsl:evaluate), schemas the unit can validate with; the processor's location demand decides AUTOMATIC. Copies keep locations, so a stylesheet's input answers under xsl:strip-space. CLI: --locations= for xpath, xquery and transform; xpath and xquery compile before they parse --context-item; an error whose value is a node prints FILE:LINE:COLUMN: the node the error names. JavaScript: createProcessor({ locations }) (not built here: no WASI SDK). 26 MB document: 173-175 MB peak without fn:location (unchanged), 249-251 MB with it or with always. XP40, XQ40 and XT40 identical case by case.

7.30 edge-case pass ( addendum): 182 cases more, 514 in 18 sets (78 new 2025-only), every construct varied by cardinality, order, errors, namespaces, text, node kinds and interaction; README tables of construct x dimension and of the standard's ambiguities; xslt3 declared as a dependency of 485 cases. SchXslt cross-check of the 369 2020 cases: 281 agree, 55 disagree (each with its clause), 18 implementation-defined, 15 not applicable. The independent check of the first 67 2025-only cases agreed (52 identical, 15 in substance); the 78 new ones wait for it. 7.30 stays unticked until then.

7.30 (): tests/schematron/, a Schematron conformance suite of sxml's own for ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025: 332 cases in 18 test sets, neutral expected results, catalog.xsd, coverage.xml (139 requirements, 131 with cases), README. SchXslt cross-check of the 265 third-edition cases: 198 agree, 49 disagree (each explained by its clause), 5 implementation-defined, 13 need a binding SchXslt lacks. The 67 2025-only cases wait for the independent check; then 7.28's gates can name the suite.

7.27 revised (), for the owner's review: the design brought in line with ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 and the owner's review. Compile errors go to a report sink (XSD's, reused); no queryBinding, xslt and xpath are read as XSLT 4.0 / XPath 4.0 ( point 2 amended), the 1.0 differences listed; binding names ignore case; an unsupported binding exits 1. Designed from the text instead of rejected: group, library and top-level extends, rules, schema and abstract-pattern params with defaults, let/@as, visit-each, severity (reports and the error-finding rule), dynamic flag/role/severity, phase from and when with #ANY, schematronEdition. The standard overturned the first version on case, library inclusion, whole-token placeholders, variable scopes, the message context and external values. Header, glossary and 7.28 (step 5b, gate 6) follow. The owner answered the eight new choices the same day and accepted ; 7.27 done. 7.28 also gives XSLT's compiler a report sink (step 1b, gate 7) and waits for 7.30's suite.

perf-8 done (): cheap coercion of one item. Matching decides no item or one item by the occurrence and the matcher's item rules without frames; coercion of one item to a plain atomic type keeps an instance at once, else atomizes a node and applies the atomic coercion rules once, with no engine, builder or repeated match; everything else takes the engine as before. SchXslt's expand stage 75.27 to 61.68 x 10^9 instructions (coercion 33 % to 18 %), about 10.5 to 8.5 s; tests/bench/coercion.xq (new, registered) 3.775 to 2.847; xmark-all unchanged. QT4 XP40 (32,785), XQ40 (46,114) and XT40 (12,185) whole, release, case by case: 0 outcomes differ. Left: untypedAtomic-to-string casts and multi-item matching ().

7.27 designed (), for the owner's review: Schematron as a front end to the XSLT AST. include/sxml/schematron.h (new, implemented by nothing yet): compile once for a phase, validate many nodes, findings as reports with the assertion's .sch location and the instance's line, column and path, SVRL written from reports. The reader builds one mode per active pattern and one template rule per rule (priority N - K; groups chain with next-match), expands includes, abstract patterns and rules while it walks, and replaces placeholders in one scan; foreign xsl: declarations go through the XSLT reader. CLI: validate --schematron --phase --format=text|json|svrl; JavaScript: compileSchematron and validate. 7.28 rewritten with its files, order and gates. Open for the owner: the 2025 constructs marked unverified (the 2025 text was not available), role and flag not inherited from the rule, xslt and xpath rejected until 7.4.

cli-4 done (): the sxml command sets no evaluation step limit (): its processor configuration asks for UINT64_MAX steps, as the header has no value for "no bound". (1 to 20000) = (1 to 20000), charged 4 x 10^8 steps, gave LIMIT_EXCEEDED and now gives true() (new CLI test). The library's default of 10^8 stays for embedders and the JavaScript package. The book's "The step limit" and three pages citing it, and docs/CLI.md "Limits", updated.

perf-9 done (): required literals in regex search. A compiled regex finds a run of characters every match contains (CODEPOINT instructions every way to MATCH passes through) and what a match can read before it; a search looks for the literal first, attempts only start positions from which the characters up to it can be read, and none when it does not occur (one step per skipped position, as before). SchXslt's expand stage 75.3 to 65.8 x 10^9 instructions (10.7 to 9.1 s), scan 12.9 % to 0.4 % of it; regex-literal.xq (new) 0.458 to 0.186 s. QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 regex sets: 0 outcomes differ; 18,000 random regexes give the same output.

perf-7 done (): faster regex matching, by four mechanisms of the one engine: ASCII member sets of classes and an ASCII category table (one bit test per ASCII character), a start filter that skips start positions no match can begin at (one step each, as before), an idle matcher kept by each regex cache entry, and character repetitions (greedy x*, x+ of one character: one step per character, two backtrack entries in all). 200,000 matches(..., "\w+\s\w+\s\d+") 0.382 to 0.197 s (contains: 0.127), 366.9 to 200.3 x 10^6 instructions at 20,000; regex-match.xq (new) 1.069 to 0.652 s; regex-reuse.xq 0.250 to 0.146 s. QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 regex sets: 0 outcomes differ.

perf-5 done (): a slice of a stored sequence shares its items (sequence slices: a cell over a vector, reported as a vector; spans of 16 items or under an eighth of the base are copied); fn:tail, fn:subsequence, fn:trunk, fn:slice and positional filters ($s[position() > N], = N to M, ...) over a vector, slice or range are O(1); a typed parameter matches a slice once its base matched (evaluation memo). 100 walks over 780 elements: position() > 1 10.23 to 0.11 s, tail 2.55 to 0.11, subsequence 3.03 to 0.11, now linear; SchXslt's expand stage 552 to 458 s. QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole: 0 outcomes differ.

perf-6 done (): the regex functions compile each regex once per evaluation, through a regex cache in the evaluation memo (4,096 entries, 8 MiB, least recently used unused entry evicted; errors and step counts per call as before). 20,000 replace calls 0.103 to 0.065 s; regex-reuse.xq (new) 0.342 to 0.247 s; bench-real.xsl 0.550 to 0.488 s; SchXslt's expand stage 555 to 551 s (compiling was under 1 %, the rest is perf-5's). QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 regex sets: 0 outcomes differ.
